headline: Funding grows. Partnerships form. Delays continue.
deck: This week, the space industry sees a mix of partnerships, funding rounds, and persistent delays.

stories.head: Fotrastra and Hadrian unite for satellite production
stories.body: Fotrastra and Hadrian are collaborating to enhance satellite production, leveraging precision machining and additive manufacturing techniques. This partnership underscores a growing trend of consolidation in the satellite manufacturing space, as companies seek efficiencies in a competitive market. The exact financial terms remain undisclosed, but the intention is clear: streamline production to meet rising demand.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where time-to-market is crucial, expect more companies to follow suit, potentially leading to fewer players but faster outputs.

stories.head: LatConnect 60 expands SWIRSAT into Malaysia and UAE
stories.body: LatConnect 60 is broadening its SWIRSAT constellation into Malaysia and the UAE, building on its existing operations in Western Australia. This expansion is part of a strategy to enhance its capabilities in satellite-based services across multiple regions. Financial specifics were not disclosed, but the move signals a growing interest in diversifying operational footprints.
stories.soWhat: As companies expand their geographic reach, the competition for local partnerships and regulatory approvals will intensify, adding layers of complexity to international operations.

stories.head: Boeing's Starliner flight schedule remains uncertain
stories.body: Boeing continues to negotiate with NASA regarding the next launch of its CST-100 Starliner, with no firm date in sight. This ongoing delay adds to the growing list of setbacks for Boeing in the commercial crew program, which has already faced significant scrutiny. The implications for NASA's broader Artemis program could be substantial, as delays in crew transport affect mission timelines.
stories.soWhat: Boeing's struggles may embolden competitors like SpaceX, further eroding confidence in Boeing's capabilities in a critical market.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's growth
watchlist.body: With a recent $190M Series C funding round, True Anomaly is positioned to expand its co-orbital security capabilities, potentially reshaping the competitive landscape.

watchlist.title: Watch for ispace's lunar mission preparations
watchlist.body: As ispace gears up for its lunar lander mission in 2028, developments could signal a shift in private lunar transportation dynamics.

watchlist.title: Monitor the impact of the FY27 budget increase
watchlist.body: The $1.4B boost to space resilience may drive new contracts and opportunities for contractors involved in national security.

watchlist.title: Expect more partnerships in satellite production
watchlist.body: Fotrastra and Hadrian's collaboration could lead to a wave of similar partnerships, as firms seek to optimize production amid rising demand.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
